newsitem.title: UK: UK utilities should see lawyers on budget - Redwood.
newsitem.headline: UK utilities should see lawyers on budget - Redwood.

text.p: Utilities singled out in this week's budget for the British government's proposed windfall profits tax should consult lawyers on whether it is legal, Conservative trade and industry spokesman John Redwood said on Monday.
"I think they must. They have a duty to shareholders," Redwood told journalists.
He said the planned tax would be a "legal minefield" and that it would be impossible for Chancellor (finance minister) Gordon Brown to frame proposals which would not be unfair to some companies.

In his Wednesday budget speech, Brown is expected to announce proposals to raise some five billion stg from a tax largely on privatised companies in the gas, electricity, water and communications sectors.
Redwood said: "Business should brace itself for a 'bash business' budget, and should start taking legal advice on the windfall tax.
"It is not permissible for ministers to slap a tax on companies and people they do not like, yet that is what this amounts to."

Redwood said he would look to see whether the tax applied to Cable and Wireless as well as British Telecommunications Plc, and to water companies which had always been private monopolies as well as those sold off under the Conservatives.

Other questions for Brown were whether the tax would be applied to profits made by businesses which had been acquired by utilities after their privatisation and whether privatised firms which were clearly not utilities such as National Freight Company were included in its net.
"If the answer to each of these questions is 'no', why is it 'no'? How can they claim it's fair?" he said.

Brown said frequently during the campaign for the May 1 election which brought Labour to power that he had taken legal advice on his windfall tax plans and had been assured that they were watertight. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
